solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New article by European about French ruler

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a Pole is a European, from Poland
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A news item about a European writing on a French leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was emperor of France, its most famous ruler.

clue.text: Is familiar with, say, patient chap's cosmetic surgery

indicators.note: say signals that the words before it are to be heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone familiar with a thing knows it
Job of the Bible is proverbial for his patience

explanation.surface: A doctor who knows a patient man has had a facial procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' reads as a medical patient, but it is the patience of Job, the biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, reshaping the nose for looks, is a common cosmetic operation.

clue.text: Fruit that's black underneath? Exactly!

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece underneath another comes after it

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone notices a fruit with a dark underside and agrees emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb as an adverb means precisely, as in plumb in the middle.

clue.text: President, inexperienced, in the shade

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was a US President
green means raw or inexperienced

explanation.surface: An untried President is sitting out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' seems to be shelter from sun, but it means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln green is a particular colour, the bright green cloth associated with Robin Hood.

clue.text: In Goa, sister's place of refuge

indicators.note: In signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A sister's retreat in Goa, the Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, and by extension any haven.

clue.text: Favouritism twice involving head of agency

indicators.note: involving means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bis is a musical or Latin word for twice, a call to repeat

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word agency

explanation.surface: An agency boss is accused twice over of playing favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a prejudice for or against someone, the same as partiality.

clue.text: Made out one politician told stories

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
telling stories is a euphemism for lying

explanation.surface: A single politician has been caught out telling tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something is to suggest or insinuate it without stating it.

clue.text: Father having name for femme fatale

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A dad takes a new name for a seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a dangerously alluring woman, after the mythical singers luring sailors.

clue.text: Fight simply, possibly without guile at first? That's most unlikely!

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way
at first takes the opening letter of guile

explanation.surface: A fighter warned to fight plainly, without trickery, doubts it will happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means 'with, on the outside': G is added to FIGHT SIMPLY before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a sarcastic way of saying something will never happen.

clue.text: Reject London football team — ultimately northern not southern

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the team name as the one changed
northern not southern means one compass letter replaces the other

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: A northerner turns down a southern London football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' and 'not' together swap the last S of SPURS for N.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with contempt, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Somebody leaving out captain?

definitions.meaning: one who skips something leaves it out
the master of a ship or leader of a team

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if the captain is being dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: One who skips is literally a skipper, and skipper is also informal for a ship's master.

clue.text: Inoculation required by Jack — a sailor

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
AB, an able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack needs a vaccination before his voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A jab is informal British slang for an injection or vaccination.

clue.text: Ibsen — so, so different and complex

indicators.note: different signals the letters are to be made into something else

explanation.surface: A critic finds Ibsen, the Norwegian playwright, so very unusual and intricate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' reads as an adjective about Ibsen but is a noun, the psychological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a complex is a fixation or preoccupation, the same as a fixation.

clue.text: Live and yearn to have a home

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Someone lives in hope, yearning for a place of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that belong somewhere have their proper place or home there.

clue.text: When upset dwelt on a disappointment

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brooding over a setback only made it feel worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-down is an anticlimax, something that fails to meet expectations.

clue.text: Concealed papers found in study after hour

indicators.note: after hour means the rest follows the hour letter

parts.note: ID is identity papers
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Secret papers are discovered in a study after an hour of searching.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden and concealed are synonyms meaning kept out of sight.

clue.text: Score a goal a game

definitions.meaning: to put the ball in the net is to score, read as two words
a team sport played with a ball and raised goal rings

explanation.surface: A goal is scored in a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, a verb and a noun: to put the ball into the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, mostly played by women in Britain and the Commonwealth.

clue.text: Experience of music fan wearing black with bully boy

parts.note: a goth is a fan of gothic rock who dresses in black
a rough is a thug or bully

explanation.surface: A black-clad fan meets a thug at a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something is to undergo or live through it.

clue.text: Man catching very quiet fish

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: guy is informal for a man
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: A fisherman silently lands a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The guppy is a small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Free from the BBC? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, the national broadcaster

explanation.surface: Something offered for nothing by the national broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free from the BBC' suggests licence-free viewing; 'Free' is a verb meaning release.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo bonds, so to set loose or release.

clue.text: A saving annual meeting of workers rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, holds a British annual conference of trade unions

explanation.surface: The union conference turns down a cost-cutting measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut in spending is a saving, a reduction in costs.

clue.text: Conservative to be defeated? It could be neck and neck

parts.note: to lose is to be defeated

explanation.surface: A Tory fears defeat in a tight election race.
explanation.definitionFit: A close contest is one where the rivals are level or nearly so.

clue.text: March — time shown in poster all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poster advertises the time of a march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a demonstration; T goes inside PROEST, from 'poster all over the place'.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a demonstration, a public march against something.

clue.text: Girl having all the plants

definitions.meaning: the plant life of a region

explanation.surface: A girl owns every plant in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is a female name and the collective term for plant life.

clue.text: American to talk continuously about the end of Nixon

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to yak is to chatter on

indicators.note: the end of means the last letter of Nixon

explanation.surface: An American chatters endlessly about how Nixon fell.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Extremely healthy or OK

definitions.meaning: in very good health, extremely fit
an expression of agreement, all right

explanation.surface: Someone is feeling in fine health and all right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means in fine health and is also a reply of agreement, like fine then.
